name_note: The GTDB genus matches the genus name used in the literature; a few genomes it contains are deposited at NCBI as Nubsella or Cytophaga.

sentences.text: A review describes Pedobacter as a genus of Gram-negative bacteria with a broad geographic distribution, isolated from habitats including water, soil, plants, wood, rocks and animals.
The same review reports that characterisation has been limited to a small number of species, while genome analyses suggest many undescribed natural products.
Pedobacter is placed in the phylum Bacteroidota and is described as a taxon known for antibiotic production that carries many uncharacterised biosynthetic gene clusters.
Reported biotechnological uses include heparinases and chondroitinases for therapeutic purposes and the antimicrobial secondary metabolites pedopeptins and isopedopeptins.
In a urinary microbiome study of systemic lupus erythematosus, Pedobacter was among genera reported to correlate negatively with proteinuria and the albumin-to-creatinine ratio.
